mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) exceeding 100k persons signals robust labor market conditions that support consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of periods with PAYEMS growth > 100k, or Rank IC < 0.05 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeds 8.0 percent, it indicates deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of UNRATE > 8.0 instances, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) indicate monetary tightening amid rising inflation, compressing equity valuations and causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in >50% of periods with FEDFUNDS↑ and CPIAUCSL↑, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS rising above 2.0% sustained for 3 months), S&P 500 forward returns turn negative over the next 20 trading days due to reduced liquidity and higher discount rates.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in >50% of monetary tightening cycles, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising trend in housing starts (HOUST) exceeding 850 thousand units reflects strong consumer demand and economic expansion, supporting corporate earnings growth and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in >50% of HOUST > 850k periods, or Rank IC < 0.05 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 800 thousand units, it signals a contraction in the housing market that reduces consumer spending and business investment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in >50% of HOUST < 800 instances, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate strong consumer demand momentum that drives corporate earnings growth, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in >50% of periods with HOUST↑ and RSAFS↑, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In an industrial contraction regime (INDPRO declining for 3 consecutive months), S&P 500 forward returns become negative over the next 5 trading days due to reduced corporate output and recessionary risks.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in >50% of industrial contraction periods, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 1-year rolling window.
